pages.text: A new girl named Fosuaa came to Class Three. She was shorter than the other nine-year-olds. Madam Esi smiled and told the class, “Fosuaa was born with dwarfism. Her bones grow in a different way, and she is just like you in every other way.”
sentences: A new girl named Fosuaa came to Class Three.
She was shorter than the other nine-year-olds.
Madam Esi smiled and told the class, “Fosuaa was born with dwarfism.
Her bones grow in a different way, and she is just like you in every other way.”
pages.alt: Inside a bright Ghanaian classroom, kind teacher Madam Esi stands warmly beside nine-year-old Fosuaa—who is shorter in stature with neat braids and yellow beads in the same school uniform—introducing her to classmates at wooden desks.

pages.text: At break time, a boy whispered, “She is a little forest spirit!” A few children giggled. Fosuaa looked down at her sandals, and her eyes filled with tears.
sentences: At break time, a boy whispered, “She is a little forest spirit!” A few children giggled.
Fosuaa looked down at her sandals, and her eyes filled with tears.
pages.alt: Out in the sunlit schoolyard at break, Fosuaa stands looking down sadly with tearful eyes while two classmates whisper at a short distance.

pages.text: Nuamah felt ashamed because he had laughed at first too. He stepped forward beside Fosuaa and raised his hand. “Stop,” he said clearly. “Her name is Fosuaa. She is a girl, not a spirit.”
sentences: Nuamah felt ashamed because he had laughed at first too.
He stepped forward beside Fosuaa and raised his hand.
“Stop,” he said clearly.
“Her name is Fosuaa.
She is a girl, not a spirit.”
pages.alt: In the schoolyard, Nuamah stands bravely right beside Fosuaa with one hand raised respectfully to stop the teasing, looking earnest and kind.

pages.text: Back in the classroom, Madam Esi spoke calmly to everyone. “Dwarfism is a medical condition. Fosuaa is a person, just like all of you. Elders tell the old forest stories with respect, and those stories are never about our classmates.”
sentences: Back in the classroom, Madam Esi spoke calmly to everyone.
“Dwarfism is a medical condition.
Fosuaa is a person, just like all of you.
Elders tell the old forest stories with respect, and those stories are never about our classmates.”
pages.alt: Back inside the quiet classroom, Madam Esi speaks gently and seriously at the front while all the children, including Fosuaa and Nuamah, sit attentively at their desks.

pages.text: After the lesson, the boy walked over to Fosuaa. “I am sorry, Fosuaa,” he said. “What I said was unkind.” Fosuaa looked up and nodded. “Thank you,” she said. “Please call me by my name.”
sentences: After the lesson, the boy walked over to Fosuaa.
“I am sorry, Fosuaa,” he said.
“What I said was unkind.” Fosuaa looked up and nodded.
“Thank you,” she said.
“Please call me by my name.”
pages.alt: By the classroom veranda, the apologetic classmate bows his head slightly with hands together saying sorry to Fosuaa, who looks up calmly with dignity while Nuamah watches warmly.

pages.text: At the next break, Fosuaa joined the skipping game. She jumped lightly and counted higher than anyone else! “Go, Fosuaa!” her classmates cheered together.
sentences: At the next break, Fosuaa joined the skipping game.
She jumped lightly and counted higher than anyone else!
“Go, Fosuaa!” her classmates cheered together.
pages.alt: Joyful sunlit schoolyard scene where two classmates turn a long skipping rope while smiling Fosuaa jumps happily in the middle and Nuamah and friends clap and cheer.

activities.question: What does Nuamah do after realising teasing is wrong?
options: Steps forward and stands up for Fosuaa

activities.question: What does Madam Esi explain about dwarfism?

items: A boy teases her at break time.
Nuamah stands up for her and Madam Esi explains.
The boy apologises and Fosuaa shines at skipping.

activities.prompt: How does it feel when someone apologises sincerely and calls you by your name?

glossary.definition: A medical condition in which a person’s bones grow differently, making them much shorter than average.
Feeling sorry and uncomfortable about something wrong you did.
Not caring or friendly; hurting someone’s feelings.
